Code's reading, the form: a sibling of scripts/m_gpwr.py importing its functions unchanged (F-5), executed from the load commit's blob. m_gpwr.compute and m_gpwr.project serve Q-F0's two arm roles, so Q-F3's six-arm projection, its three bars and its three guards are composed here from m_gpwr's functions (launch_count, looks_for, guard_block, rec, dec, fs) and mf3's (schedule.interleave, schedule._n90_exact, keys, bars); the self-test asserts the composition equal to m_gpwr's own figures at Q-F0's two arms. No attribute of an m or mf3 module is substituted.

Code's reading of F-5's "A1 96/32": it is m:184's cached floor. Q-F3 runs uncached since G-ID-F3's FAIL (LOCK-m-F3 v0.2 §3, "path = uncached"); m:184 gives A1's floor as "96 cached, 80 uncached / 32" (m:230: "A1 floor 80"; mf3's schedule.FLOORS; the analyzer's F3_PLANNED). So A1 runs at 80/32, in the power (.878) and the launch rule alike; m:190's figure at 96/32 (.916) is printed beside and used nowhere.

Code's reading of the power floors (m:190): A1, a control, needs >= .85 at P = .70 and alpha .01; A2 needs >= .85 at P = .65 and alpha .01; A3, the screen, has no floor, and its POSITIVE probability at alpha .05 and P = .65 is reported, not gated. Each figure is the analyzer's f3_power_block at the planned floors. m:190's raise is not triggered; had A1 or A2 fallen below .85, this program would STOP and escalate, applying neither the raise nor the grid rule for A2/A3.

Code's reading of the launch rule (m:192): r = 29/40 is one rate for the unit, pooled over all 40 (m:297); each arm's L is m_gpwr.launch_count at its own floor and its own balance unit (mf3's schedule.UNIT_SIZE: 32 for A1 and A1s, 16 for A2 to A3s), cross-checked against mf3's schedule._n90_exact. The rows for k = 1..40 are computed the same way and checked against m:234-241's rows (the hours column at m:230's basis included) and m:243's line after them; looks = ceil(total / 40), checked against m:330's uncached list.

Code's reading of the projection: mf3's schedule.interleave over keys.TEMPLATES (A1, A1s, A2, A2s, A3, A3s). The live arm with the fewest launches goes next, ties to table order, and an arm leaves the rotation for good at its stop. Each arm launches to its L. Looks fall at every 40th launch and at the end, and an end on a multiple adds no look (m:330; m_gpwr.project's form, over six arms).

Code's reading of how the three bars' domains are pooled: each bar is cumulative over its own domain, with one count per look (m:330), at its own p0 and alpha from mf3's bars, by valence_core.m.bars' critical_k and seq_false_pause (as mf3's bars import them). round_degeneracy counts the three sham arms' task rounds (A1s + A2s + A3s; 10 per sham launch; p0 .05). reasoning_line_defect counts the same three arms' reasoning lines (6 per sham launch; p0 .10). own_pair_lexical counts A2s + A3s task rounds (10 per launch; p0 .02). No contrast-arm unit enters a bar's n (m:271's sham domain; m:330). crit_j at each look is checked against the mf3 bar's own evaluate().

Code's reading of Q7 (a)'s floor case, its Q-F0 reading kept: the three sham arms leave the rotation at their floors, computed at ceil(floor / r), which is 45, 78 and 78 at r = 29/40, and at the floor itself, 32, 56 and 56. Every contrast arm launches to its L. Both keep 10 rounds and 6 lines per sham launch, which over-counts the units of the sessions they assume end early at an exclusion. The guards move with the sham arms' launches and are recomputed in both.

Code's reading of Q7 (a)'s realised case, carried to Q-F3: G-F3's realised counts over its 24 sham sessions, 189 of <= 240 task rounds and 98 of <= 144 reasoning lines (the G-F3 entry; the seat's §A.1), taken as pooled rates per sham launch, 189/24 = 63/8 rounds and 98/24 = 49/12 lines. Each rate applies alike to every sham launch of each bar's domain, own_pair_lexical's A2s + A3s rounds at the same 63/8. Only the three bars are recomputed there; the guards count launches, which the case does not move.

Code's reading of the realised case's rounding: the cumulative count at a look, launches x rate, is not whole at every look. Each is rounded to the nearest whole unit, a half up (floor(x + 1/2)), before the bar is evaluated. The rounded counts are non-decreasing, and their unrounded values are recorded beside (n_j_exact).

Code's reading of the guard's binding halves: the guard is figured per contrast arm against its matched sham (m:316; keys.PAIRS: A1-A1s, A2-A2s, A3-A3s), each pair's cumulative launches per look passed to m_gpwr's guard functions in its arm roles (the contrast as A0, the sham as A0s). Both halves bind on Qwen (m:316; mf3's bars' binding flags, read), so the pausing figure is the union, each half's own figure beside: the absolute half exact at p0 .20 over the contrast arm's launches; the Fisher half at the common null rate .20, with the grid j/100, its refined maximum (+/- .01 by .001) and the union's maximum over common rates <= .20 (Code's Q-F0 reading, kept), the grid and the maxima figured on the projection only. Each pair's figure is its own. The unit's figure, m:285's "the exclusion guard's false-pause figure" for a unit whose guard runs per contrast arm, is the probability that some pair's guard pauses, 1 - (1 - u_A1)(1 - u_A2)(1 - u_A3), each u its pair's pausing figure at the common rate 1/5: exact under Q7 (b)'s model, the three pairs sharing no session; it is figured in every case the guards are.

Code's reading of the joint (Q7 (c), adapted to Q-F3's three bars and its guard of three pairs): the joint figure is each bar's own (projection case), with the guard's beside: each pair's union and the unit's figure. The joint over the three bars, and over the bars and the guard, is not computed (the sentence under JOINT). The hair triggers carry no p0 and have no figure.

Code's reading of the hours basis: §A.7's "m:205's basis" is read as the unit's own pre-registered basis line. m:205 is Q-F0's and the OLMo checkpoints' line and holds no Q-F3 figure; m:230 is Q-F3's uncached one, 641.6-713.6 s per session, applied to the unit's total (m:192: "hours = the unit's total × the basis named"), with m:238's column, 148-165 h, as its oracle. §A.5's figures are printed beside, by citation of the seat's raw (its path, commit and sha256; each row verbatim), as the realised basis of record. This program recomputes none of them.

Code's reading of LOOK_EVERY and of what this program opens: LOOK_EVERY is mf3's resume.LOOK_EVERY, which is m's (its committed source lines "from valence_core.m import resume as m_resume" and "LOOK_EVERY = m_resume.LOOK_EVERY", each required verbatim), read from valence_core.m.resume. valence_core.mf3.resume is not imported, because its import (through valence_core.m.corr) opens a file under data/, and this program opens nothing under data/.
